title: Runek world
description: A Runek world as data: world settings plus a tree of component nodes. See https://runek.nullorder.org/docs/worlds-as-data

timezone.description: IANA zone for a live, clock-driven day/night.

controls.description: Input remap: action to KeyboardEvent.code values.

fonts.description: Font URLs by role, and fallback fonts for characters a role lacks.

fallback.description: Fonts tried in order for characters the role font lacks.

stream.description: Mount only the nodes near the viewer, for dense worlds: true, or { radius, cell } in units.

build.description: Mount components that have a build function without React.

luminance.description: How bright glowing surfaces are, per kind, relative to diffuse white (1 is face value).

props.AcousticPanel.description: A fabric-wrapped acoustic absorber panel proud of a slim frame, wall-mounted from its back like Poster, or turned face down as a ceiling cloud. Seeded fabric. Decorative.

color.description: The fabric. Seeded from muted studio colours when unset.

props.AcUnit.description: An outdoor AC unit on a wall bracket with its drain hose, optionally in a wire cage. Drawn by the world's shared facade-kit meshes, so any number cost no extra draws. Decorative: no collider.

color.description: Body color. Seeded when unset.

accent.description: Side-art stripe and marquee glow. Seeded when unset.

on.description: Lit screen showing the game; off, dark glass.

game.description: Which game is running; each is laid out from the seed. Invaders when unset.

players.description: Control sets on the panel (one or two players). Seeded when unset.

props.Billboard.description: A board that runs ads as data: one or two lines of lettering in the world's display font beside a mark drawn in code that moves with the world clock (steam off a bowl, a watch's hands, a cell filling), cut to the next every `hold` seconds through torn strips. Its picture is redrawn only while near the camera. Lit at the world's screen luminance level. Decorative: no collider.

accent.description: The second line, the tagline and the mark's highlights.

props.BladeSign.description: A board standing out from a wall with one word stacked down both faces in the world's display font, lit at the world's sign luminance level, with tube edges. Drawn by the world's shared facade-kit meshes. Decorative: no collider.

position.description: Bottom of the board at the wall [x, y, z] in units. The board stands out along local +Z.

rotation.description: Rotation [x, y, z] in radians. Turn about Y so local +Z points out of the wall.

gap.description: Gap between the wall and the board, in units.

tube.description: Run a tube down both edges of the board.

props.Book.description: A single procedural book — standing, lying, or open — with a seeded cover and optional click interaction; the standalone sibling of Bookshelf's instanced spines.

position.description: Position [x, y, z] in units (1 unit = 1 m, Y-up).

rotation.description: Euler rotation [x, y, z] in radians.

width.description: Cover width (spine to fore-edge), in units.

pose.description:
`lying` rests on its back cover (spine on the -x edge); `standing` stands
upright on its bottom edge; `open` lies opened flat at the spine.

color.description: Cover color. Defaults to a seeded cloth-bound color.

title.description: Shown as a hover label when the book is interactive.

href.description: Navigated to on click when no `onSelect` is given.

reach.description:
How close the player's avatar (its eyes) must be to hover or click the book, in units.
Only applies while a `Player` is mounted; with a free camera it's always in reach.

seed.description: Seed for the deterministic variation: same seed, same result.

props.Bookshelf.description: Procedurally generated bookshelf with seeded books and one cuboid collider.

position.description: Position [x, y, z] in units (1 unit = 1 m, Y-up).

rotation.description: Euler rotation [x, y, z] in radians.

depth.description: Depth, in units.

shelves.description: Number of rows. Defaults to 3; set 1 or 2 for a shorter case.

fill.description:
Fraction of shelf space filled with procedural decoration, 0–1. Defaults to
`0` (an empty shelf); set it for a decorative, non-interactive shelf. Ignored
when `books` is set.

color.description: Frame color. Defaults to the world palette's `wood` slot.

backColor.description: Back-panel color. Defaults to the world palette's `woodDark` slot.

seed.description: Seed for the deterministic variation: same seed, same result.

books.description:
Explicit, addressable books. When provided, these replace the procedural
`fill` and are the only books rendered. Pass `[]` for an empty shelf and
append to make books appear. A book is clickable when `onBookSelect` is set
or it carries an `href`.

reach.description:
How close the player's avatar (its eyes) must be to a book to hover or click it, in units.
Only applies while a `Player` is mounted; with a free camera every book is in reach.

label.description:
Section label rendered above the shelf, e.g. `"Guides"`. Drawn as a `Sign`
in the world's `display` face.

labelColor.description: Label color. Defaults to the world palette's `accent` slot.

color.description: Spine color. Defaults to a seeded color.

href.description: Navigated to on click when no `onBookSelect` is given.

shelf.description:
Row to place the book on, counted from the top (0 = top row). Clamped to
the shelf's row count. Books without a row auto-pack bottom-up around the
placed ones.

lightColor.description: The light and the glowing bulb.

reach.description:
How far its light carries, in units. The world lends its few real lights by strength over
the square of distance, never nearer than this reach, so a short reach makes a dim fitting
win while the viewer is in its room and give the light back once they leave. Keep it near
the room's size.

light.description:
Ask the world for a real light. Off, it still glows: a big room wants many lit fittings
and only a few real lights, fewer than the world's light budget.

north.description:
World yaw (radians) the dial reads as north, using the same convention as `Player`/`Helm`
yaw: 0 faces +Z, so the default makes +Z north (and -X east).

props.Crowd.description: People on a street in bulk: hooded figures in long coats walking their lanes there and back, each with one small light at the collar, stepping round the player. lanes.description:
The paths they walk, in the node's frame. A walker keeps to one lane, going to its end and
back. One 16-unit lane along X by default.

speed.description: Slowest and fastest a walker goes, in units a second.

spread.description: How far to either side of its lane a walker keeps, in units, so a crowd is not a queue.

berth.description: How far round the player a walker steps aside, in units. 0 for none.

props.Person.description: A sculpted, clothed, skinned figure generated from a seed: one continuous body with a sculpted face, lidded eyes that follow you, and hands with fingers, in four style templates (stylized by default, realistic, anime, and punk, drawn in flat two-tone color inside an ink line). Bodies are built in layers (frame, muscle, soft tissue) in seven builds. Every part is configurable as plain JSON: the body (build, tone, height), the face (eyes, brows, nose, lips, blush), hair, and clothing as ordered layers (shirts, sweaters, vests, coats, jackets, crop tops, tanks, dresses, robes, trousers, jeans, cargos, skirts, pleated skirts, stockings, shoes, boots, sneakers, belts, scarves, capes, and street wear with lit trims) that fit any body. Role presets, swappable cosmetic skins, hats and accessories, poses, idle breathing and blinking. Give it a patrol or a wander radius and it walks: a route that is a pure function of the clock, following the ground, with a walk cycle and a step aside for the player and other walkers. A route with a departure time is a one-way trip (to a desk, to bed) that reports its arrival, and actions put a key prompt over it (Talk, Info) when the player comes near. Meshes build in the background, coarse first, with full detail near the camera. Its skeleton answers to the VRM humanoid bone names, so a pose source (a clip library, poses off the network) can drive it in place of the walk cycle. Place one at a spawn point, or use it as the Player's third-person body.

style.description:
Proportion and face template: `stylized` (default) is an animated-film look with a big
head and eyes, small features, and slender limbs; `realistic` keeps canonical human
proportions; `anime` pushes the eyes and legs further; `punk` is drawn the way an animator
would, with long legs, tall flat eyes under a lash line, hair in chunky locks, and flat
two-tone color inside an ink line (no ink line under `WebGPURenderer`).

anatomy.description:
How much of the body is built: `bones` is the bare frame, `muscle` the frame with its
muscles on, `surface` (default) the finished body. For looking at how a build is put
together, with `clothes={[]}`.

kind.description: Role preset: fills `outfit`, `hat`, and `accessories` unless you set them.

gender.description: Silhouette cues only; every trait it influences stays overridable. Seeded when unset.

age.description: Head-to-body ratio, stature, and (for `elder`) a stooped spine.

body.description:
The body: `build`, skin `tone`, and `height`. The flat props below are shorthands for
the same fields; when both are set, this object wins.

face.description:
The face, part by part: eye color and size, brow color and weight, nose shape, lip
color and fullness, blush.

clothes.description:
Clothing layers, inner to outer, each with its own type, color, and options. The order
decides the fit: a shirt listed before the jeans is tucked in. Replaces `outfit`; `[]`
is the bare base body (a smooth mannequin).

height.description: Standing height, in units. Every other measurement derives from it.

build.description: Limb thickness and torso depth. Seeded when unset.

skinTone.description: Skin color; seeded from a curated set of tones when unset.

skin.description:
Cosmetic loadout: a preset name from `PERSON_SKINS` (e.g. `"winter"`) or a custom
`PersonSkin` bundle. Individual props win over it. Plain JSON either way, so an editor
or an in-world UI can swap a figure's whole look by writing this one prop.

hair.description: A style name, or `{ style, color }`.

outfit.description: One-word outfit; expands to a `clothes` stack (e.g. `tunic`: trousers, tunic, shoes).

topColor.description:
Outermost top's color; defaults to a seeded shade of a palette slot. A garment's own
`color` wins over it.

bottomColor.description: Bottoms' color; defaults to a seeded shade of the palette's `woodDark`, `stone`, or `metal`.

shoeColor.description: Footwear color; defaults to the palette's `metal`.

trimColor.description:
The lit seams and stripes of street clothes (`runner`, `shell`, `rig`, `street`, a hoodie's
cords) and a visor's slit. Defaults to a lamp color picked by the seed. They shine on a
`punk` figure and are plain color on the others.

pose.description:
What the figure is doing when it isn't walking. `sit` and `type` need a seat under them
(`type` is seated at a desk, fingers tapping); `work` leans over a counter; `play` works
controls at waist height; `drink` holds a mug and sips from it now and then; `lie` lies on its
back centered on `position`, head toward local -Z, so it takes a `Bed`'s position and
rotation at mattress height.

patrol.description:
Walk these waypoints, relative to `position` and turning with `rotation`, in units.
Height follows the ground; a waypoint's y lifts the figure above it.

wander.description:
Wander a seeded loop of five points within this radius of `position`, in units. `patrol`
wins when both are set.

speed.description: Walking speed, in units per second. Defaults by age: child 1.0, adult 1.3, elder 0.8.

pause.description: Seconds held at each waypoint. Walking always stands; the authored `pose` plays here.

loop.description: `loop` walks from the last waypoint back to the first; `pingpong` retraces the route.

route.description:
A one-way trip through these waypoints, relative to `position` like `patrol`, setting off
at `departAt`. Before then the figure waits at the first point facing its `rotation`; after
the last it stays there, facing the way it came, in its `pose`. Wins over `patrol` and
`wander`. Give a new trip a new `position` (the old one's end) and `departAt`.

departAt.description:
When the `route` trip sets off, in epoch milliseconds on the world's clock
(`useWorld().now()`, which is `Date.now()` unless the world is given a clock). Plain data, so
every viewer sees the figure at the same point of its trip. Unset, the trip is long over.

gait.description:
Walk-cycle speed, in units per second, for a figure something else moves (a cart, a
script). Unset, a route drives it, and a `Player`'s body walks at the avatar's speed.

lookAt.description:
Turn the head (and eyes) toward the player's avatar (or the camera, when no `Player` is
mounted) when it comes within `lookRadius`.

lookRadius.description: How close the avatar must be for `lookAt` to engage, in units.

bubble.description:
A short line in a speech bubble over the head (what the figure is saying or doing right
now). Long lines wrap and are cut after a few.

emote.description:
A small animated sign over the head: `sleep` (rising z's), `alert` (a bouncing !), `think`
(pulsing dots), `happy` (a heart), `coffee` (a steaming cup).

actions.description:
What the player can do with this figure (`Talk`, `Info`). When the avatar comes within
`actionRadius` a prompt shows them over the head, with the key each world `controls`
action is bound to; pressing one calls `onAction` with its `id`. Only the nearest figure
(or other `Interactable`) in range shows a prompt and takes the key.

actionRadius.description: How close the avatar must come for `actions`, in units.

collider.description: Capsule collider, so the figure is something you bump into.

physics.description:
Render as a bare visual with no `RigidBody`: for a parent that owns the physics
(e.g. as `Player`'s third-person avatar). When false, `collider` is ignored.

detail.description:
`auto` builds the full-detail mesh only within ~10 units of the camera; `high` always;
`low` never.

props.Player.description: First/third-person character controller (ecctrl wrapper). WASD moves; mouse-drag or the arrow keys steer the camera in either view. The body it carries turns to face the way it walks, and its motion (speed, distance, heading, jumps, where the camera looks) is published every frame for that body and for net code. Reads the world's `avatar` setting for its default view and the world's `controls` for key bindings.

view.description:
Camera view: `first` (through the avatar's eyes), `third` (behind it), or `overhead` (high
above at a fixed tilt, following it; scroll zooms, WASD walks relative to the screen). Unset
defers to the world default (`<World avatar>`); falls back to first-person. An explicit value
here always wins. A world `view` control (e.g. `controls: { view: ['KeyV'] }`) cycles the
three at runtime.

height.description: How tall the avatar is, feet to crown, in meters: the length of its capsule.

eyeHeight.description:
Eye height above the feet, in meters: where the first-person camera sits, what the
third-person camera turns about, and what others look at when they look at the player.
Unset, just under the top of the capsule as it floats (about 1.4 at the default size).

sprintSpeed.description: Top speed while the `run` key is held, in meters per second.

cameraDistance.description:
How far behind the avatar the third-person camera starts, in meters; scrolling zooms from
there.

fov.description:
How wide the first-person view is, in degrees across, on a 16:9 screen. The default,
140, takes in most of what both eyes see, so the world wraps around you instead of
sitting behind a window. Like most games it follows the screen's shape, not its size: a
wider screen (an ultrawide or curved monitor) keeps the same angle top to bottom and sees
more across, up to 200°; a narrower one sees less across, down to 110°, then holds that
and opens up top to bottom, until a tall phone screen just shows less across. It is drawn
through a gently curved (Panini) lens: true to life straight ahead, the sides squeezed in
rather than stretched as a flat camera would. Third-person and overhead keep the world
camera's own lens.

peripheralBlur.description:
How blurred the very edge of the first-person view is, in CSS pixels, easing to sharp
toward the centre the way peripheral vision does; turn to look at something and it comes
into focus. 0 turns it off.

The real light comes from the world's light pool. One thin collider for the pole.

props.Tower.description: A procedural city tower from a seeded shape grammar: podium, setback, shaft and crown, with street, service, podium, tower and crown bands drawn by one shared facade shader (shop bays, lit windows with rooms behind them, trims, posters and leaks), so towers batch. Four eras (concrete, tenement, glass, makeshift) set the massing and dressing. Faces listed in `frontage` get relief and the facade kit: shop names, blade and roof signs, awnings, shutters, AC units, pipes, vending machines, cables across the street and light pooled on the pavement. Lit after dusk at the world's luminance levels. Colliders over the footprint and along each street face.

position.description: Position of the tower's base centre [x, y, z] in units (1 unit = 1 m, Y-up).

trim.description: Neon trim along the parapets and crown, and the color of the tower's main sign, lit at the world's `sign` luminance level. `"none"` for a plain tower. Seeded when unset.

cornerStrips.description: Also run the trim colour up the corners.

shopfronts.description: Shop bays along the ground floor.

era.description: Which era built it: `concrete` (squat, heavy, stencilled), `tenement` (balconies, sign frames, drum lanterns), `glass` (a thin glass slab with a clock in its crown) or `makeshift` (cages, shacks, cable). Seeded among the first, second and last when unset.

podium.description: Podium height in units, for a tower tall and wide enough to have a shaft (at least 34 high and 10 across). Seeded between 15 and 25 when unset.

frontage.description: The faces that front a street: `+z`, `+x`, `-z`, `-x` in the tower's own frame. Each gets piers, a fascia, signs and the instanced kit props, and the first one listed carries the tower's big sign. Empty by default, so a tower costs one merged mesh until it is told where the street is.
